lens: sceptic-realtime: checks for look-ahead bias, timing and data artefacts. I audited realtime_min_lag_q against the catalog release lags and publication practice. I rebuilt every Orkla-weighted composite with prior-year (truly real-time) and fixed geographic weights, validated against the panel to a maximum difference of 1e-4. I also re-ran the claim tests with M&A/definition/Easter/VAT/India controls, base-effect controls for y/y targets, stricter lags, and my own expanding-window OOS engine (eval 2010Q1-2026Q2, no training on 2020Q1-21Q2).

verdicts.corrected_statement: EU packaging PPI is the strongest same-quarter margin correlate: -0.15pp d_margin per 1pp (HAC t -9.6 full; -3.1 ex 2021Q3-23Q4; -3.0 at real-time h=0 using the previous quarter). The 2021-23 episode supplies about 70% of the covariance. The raw-material (local-currency) effect is a two-episode result. Full sample: a sustained +10pp gives about -0.5pp (avg lags 0-3, t -2.75). Outside 2021-23 the effect is not statistically established (t -1.2), and it vanishes once 2007Q2-Q4 is dummied (t -0.3).
verdicts.evidence: (a) Timing. packaging_eu_yoy and plastic PPI are lag 1 (Eurostat about 35 days), which is correct. Real-time h=0 (feature t-1): -0.14 (t -5.8) full, -0.17 (t -3.0) ex-episode. At h=1: ex t -1.5. (c) Weights. raw_mat_wloc rebuilt with prior-year or fixed weights correlates 0.999 with the published series. The avg L0-3 coefficient is -0.053 under all three weight sets (t -2.70 to -2.75), and the DL profile is unchanged to within 0.05pp per 10pp. (d) M&A and definitions. Packaging ex-episode with pure M&A dummies (Bakers, Rieber, Hame, Eastern, SladCo, Krupskaya): t -3.05. Ex India quarters: t -4.7. Ex 2007Q2-09Q2: t -3.7. Easter controls: no change. With all event dummies including a 2007 dummy and covid: b -0.094, t -2.18. Raw materials ex-episode: -0.026 (t -1.21). With a 2007Q2-Q4 dummy alone: -0.01 (t -0.31). With all events: t -0.23. Ex 2007Q2-09Q2: t -1.56. The 2007 quarters also contain the MTR (India) and Krupskaya acquisitions and the definition-A CEE/Russia exposure.
verdicts.residual_doubt: The mechanism lens used cubic PDLs over 12 lags, and its K12 ex-episode p=0.013 could reflect long-lag structure that my simpler summaries miss. The packaging ex-episode t of about -3 sits right at the honest threshold.

verdicts.corrected_statement: The fast half holds: +10pp raw-material inflation lowers d_margin by about 1.0-1.1pp within 1-2 quarters (about 0.8-0.9pp ex-episode), robust to M&A dummies and real-time weights. The slow half does not: the delayed gain from cost decreases (+0.4 to +1.1pp by lag 6) is created by M&A quarters. With pure M&A dummies it becomes -0.45pp (full) and -0.24pp (ex-episode).
verdicts.evidence: Quadratic PDL over lags 0-6, positive and negative parts of raw_mat_wloc. Without dummies: pos10 at L1-2 = -1.06/-1.07 (full) and -0.92/-0.78 (ex); neg10 at L6 = +0.41 (full) and +1.05 (ex), which replicates the claim. With pure M&A dummies: pos10 L2 = -1.12/-0.91 (kept); neg10 L6 = -0.45/-0.24. With a Rieber 2013Q2-14Q1 dummy alone: neg10 L6 = -0.14/+0.45. The unrestricted DL agrees: neg10 L6 goes from +0.46/+0.97 to -0.27/-0.07 with M&A dummies and to -0.79/-0.30 with all events. With prior-year weights, all figures stay within 0.1pp. Bakers 2012 alone does not drive it (+0.96/+1.29).
verdicts.residual_doubt: Rieber's dilution coincides with a cost-cycle turn, so the dummy may absorb some genuine cost effect. Decreasing-cost episodes are few (2009, 2012-13, 2019-20, 2023-24), so the decrease side is weakly identified whatever the specification.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Lagged (5-7 quarter) cost and price inflation is positively related to d_margin in sample, and this survives base-effect controls. SE food PPI at t-6: +0.08-0.09pp per 1pp, t 3.0-4.5 full and ex-episode. EU dairy PPI t 3.1-4.2. The effect is recovery from the earlier transitory dip, not lasting catch-up: in the 2-year margin change the full-sample effect is insignificant (t 1.3-1.4). Its real-time forecasting value is modest. SE food PPI at t-6 cuts RMSE by 6-9% at h=1-4 only ex-episode (CW p 0.02-0.04), with no gain over the full sample (ratio 0.99-1.02). SE CPI at t-6 adds nothing out of sample.
verdicts.evidence: (a) Timing. The PPIs are lag 1, so x(t-6) is available at every horizon up to h=5, which is valid. (e) The screen's own-lag control was d_margin(t-7), not the base d_margin(t-4). Adding d_margin(t-4): dairy t 3.5 (full) / 4.2 (ex). Adding d_margin(t-4..t-6): 3.1/3.7. Adding the base plus x(t-2): 3.0/3.4. SE food PPI: 3.0-4.0. Packaging at k=6 does not survive the base control (full t 1.55). Target d_m(t)+d_m(t-4): dairy full t 1.4, ex 2.8; SE food PPI 1.3 / 2.8. (d) Dummies and sub-periods. Ex 2007-09: dairy t 4.8, SE food PPI 5.3. 2010+ ex-episode: 4.9 / 4.2. With all event dummies: dairy t 2.5, SE food PPI 3.2-4.2. (e) Episode share of covariance: 10% (dairy) and 1% (SE food PPI). OOS, AR(t-h-1, t-4) base: SE food PPI ratios ex-episode 0.913-0.938, full 0.994-1.009. Dairy ex-episode 0.96-0.99.
verdicts.residual_doubt: The k=5-7 lag was selected from a scan of 7 lags × 200 features. The full-sample OOS failure means the signal mispredicts the 2023-24 rebound.

verdicts.corrected_statement: 4Q changes in 10y yields are strongly negative for d_margin: NO -0.99pp per +1pp, t -4.9; Orkla-weighted -0.93, t -5.1. They are the best full-sample OOS single predictor (RMSE ratio 0.93 at h=0, 0.90 at h=1), and that OOS gain disappears outside 2021Q3-23Q4 (1.01 / 1.00). The in-sample relation does not disappear, however: ex-episode -0.84 (t -3.6), with packaging and agri controls -0.79 (t -3.7), and also excluding 2007-09 -0.64 (t -3.4). So the data do not establish that the variable is only a proxy for the 2021-23 cost shock. The channel is unidentified.
verdicts.evidence: (a) Yields are lag 0 (OECD monthly averages, about 5 days), which is valid. (c) w_gov10y_d4 with prior-year or fixed weights: coefficient -0.94/-0.95 vs -0.93 for the published composite. OOS ratios 0.932-0.933 vs 0.934 at h=0. Ex-episode in-sample t -3.0 to -2.9. OOS with my engine: NO yields at h=0 give 0.931 (CW p 0.048) full, 1.013 ex, 1.053 ex-infl-and-covid. At h=1: 0.901 (p 0.023) full, 0.997 ex. 2010+ ex-episode in-sample: -0.78 (t -2.8).
verdicts.residual_doubt: Yields are persistent and the in-sample ex-episode t of 3.4-3.7 is only modestly above the honest threshold. The relation could still proxy the business or disinflation cycle rather than any rate effect.

verdicts.corrected_statement: There is no robust evidence that a weaker SEK lowers Orkla Foods margins, or that EUR/SEK is a useful real-time d_margin nowcast. In sample, same-quarter EUR/SEK gives -0.16pp per 10% (t -0.6), and -0.3pp controlling for USD food prices (t -1.1). A small OOS gain (R² +0.03 all, +0.06 ex-episode vs base) appears only against the weak AR(t-1)+Easter benchmark. It disappears against AR(t-1, t-4): ratio 1.007, CW p 0.13. Management's weak-SEK mentions do coincide with EUR/SEK +5.6% vs -0.5%, but those quarters had higher, not lower, d_margin (+0.36 vs -0.01pp).
verdicts.evidence: (a) EUR/SEK is lag 0 (daily), so timing is fine. Replication of the mechanism spec (PDL L0-6 plus AR(t-1) + Easter window, expanding window from 2010, with or without covid training quarters): ratio 0.986 / R² +0.028 (CW p 0.065) all, 0.969 / +0.061 (p 0.022) ex-episode, 1.003 for 2015+. This is weaker than the claimed +0.06/+0.09 with p 0.011/0.002. (e) The gain comes from the 7-lag PDL standing in for the omitted seasonal own lag d_margin(t-4): with that lag in the base, the ratio is 1.006-1.007 and h=1 is 1.09. L0-only and L0-1 versions are worse than the base (1.014-1.035). In-sample with event dummies: t -0.55. Text: 25 fx_weak quarters replicated (EUR/SEK 5.57 vs -0.48). The text is an ex-post explanation printed in the same report as the margin, so it is not a predictor.
verdicts.residual_doubt: The mechanism lens's lag-1 trough (-0.82pp, controlling for USD commodities) used a different specification that I did not fully replicate. A small SEK cost effect hidden by translation or hedging cannot be excluded.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Out of sample (expanding from 2010, AR(t-h-1, t-4) base), no single macro predictor robustly beats the AR for d_margin. Packaging (lag 1) at h=0 gives RMSE 0.965 (CW p 0.07) full and 0.982 (p 0.018) ex-episode; plastic PPI 0.947 / 0.961. These were picked ex post, so they are upper bounds. Real wages, confidence, policy-rate levels, energy and nominal wages have no positive or forecastable margin effect. Ex-episode there are small negative in-sample associations for confidence (-0.5 to -0.65pp per SD, t -2.4 to -3.2) and real wages (t -1.9 to -3.1), with no OOS gain (ratios 0.97-1.15).
verdicts.evidence: (a) All lags valid: LCI 77 days (lag 1), EC and Finans Norge confidence (lag 0), policy rates (lag 0), energy (lag 0). Energy ex-episode |t| ≤ 1.4 (electricity, gas, Brent). Nominal wage |t| ≤ 1.2. Policy-rate level |t| ≤ 0.6. Confidence OOS ratio 0.999-1.025 at h=0 and 1.006-1.146 at h=1. Real wage OOS 1.08 full, 0.97-0.99 ex-episode (CW p 0.02-0.05). Model selection used full-sample RMSE (ex-post picks), so the claimed 4-7% gains are optimistic.
verdicts.residual_doubt: The negative ex-episode confidence and real-wage t-stats (about -3) sit near the d_margin honest threshold. My placebo puts that threshold lower for d_margin (t95 about 2.0-2.35), so a weak countercyclical association cannot be excluded.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Organic growth co-moves with Orkla-weighted food CPI ex VAT, at about 0.55-0.6pp per 1pp (t 8.5 full), and this is unaffected by real-time weights, definition dummies, India, distribution deals, the 2026Q2 VAT cut or Easter. Ex 2021Q3-23Q4 (t 2.4-3.6), the evidence comes from the 2008-10 food-price cycle. Excluding 2008-10 as well: 0.21, t 0.8. Using quality-A quarters only, ex-episode: t 1.1. So pass-through is evidenced in the two inflation episodes, not in normal times. Orkla's reported price component 2022Q2-26Q2 = -0.23 + 0.97 × CPI ex VAT (R² 0.85; Nordic slope 1.27, R² 0.91; food PPI lagged 1q slope 0.77, R² 0.90), but this rests on one cycle (n=17). Four of those points were published only as later comparatives, and 2025 sits 2.6pp below the line.
verdicts.evidence: (c) Prior-year weights: 0.565 (t 8.7) full, 0.632 (t 2.8) ex. Fixed weights: 0.573 / 0.593. (d) Ex-episode with definition dummies: 0.65 (t 3.2). With a 2015-16 distribution dummy: 0.72 (t 3.3). Ex India quarters: 0.76 (t 3.6). India-blended CPI: 0.68 (t 3.0). Ex 2026Q2: 0.551 (t 8.4) full. Q3/Q4 only, ex-episode: 0.79 (t 3.9). Ex-episode and ex 2007Q2-09Q2: 0.62 (t 1.7). Ex 2008-10: 0.21 (t 0.81). (a) Real-time nowcast: Nordic lag 0 gives 0.55 (t 2.7) ex-episode; Orkla-weighted lag 1 gives 0.48 (t 2.1). Episode share of covariance: 70%. Price component: replicated exactly. Quarters printed in their own report only (2023Q2+, n=13): slope 1.22, R² 0.77. Price-component residual for 2026Q2: +0.65 with the VAT adjustment, +1.96 on the VAT-inclusive CPI (the SE food CPI is -6.5% incl. VAT). Prior-year weights give the same price fit (R² 0.854).
verdicts.residual_doubt: The ex-VAT adjustment assumes full and immediate VAT pass-through. The 2008 og values are mostly quality B ('about'), and 2008 is the first year of definition B, so the second episode is measured with noise.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Selling-price expectation surveys do not lead organic growth in a robust real-time sense. The in-sample lead of EA food-industry selling-price expectations (d4) on d_og at h=4 (t 5.2 full, 5.3 ex-episode, replicated) is a base effect. Controlling for the base og(t-4) leaves t 2.7 full and 0.9 ex-episode. For og levels with own lags the survey adds nothing ex-episode at h=1/2/4 (t 0.4/0.9/1.3). OOS gains of 3-10% RMSE come entirely from 2021Q3-23Q4. Ex-episode ratios are 0.99-1.05 for all six survey variants.
verdicts.evidence: (a) Timing. EC surveys are released before month end (lag 0) and SSB BTS about 22 days after quarter end (lag 1), so the panel lags are valid. The relevant base og(t-4) is published only 2-6 weeks after the h=4 origin. (e) At h=1 and h=2, adding og(t-4) takes the d_og t from 3.6/5.9 to 1.2/2.0 (full) and to -0.5/0.1 (ex-episode). The weighted level and d4 versions behave the same: ex-episode t ≤ 2.4 after the base control. (c) Prior-year-weight versions of w_ec_food_ind_sell_price_exp give the same OOS ratios to within 0.003. My OOS, og target, AR base: EA level h=1/2 gives 0.949/0.929 full and 1.029/1.034 ex. NIER grocery 0.928 full, 1.008 ex. SSB 0.901 full, 1.011 ex. EC series are seasonally adjusted and revised; d4 transforms are largely immune to that.
verdicts.residual_doubt: The surveys do help within the 2021-23 episode (and lead Orkla's reported price by 2-3 quarters there), so they may matter in the next inflation shock. Ten episode quarters cannot establish this.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Real-wage growth relates negatively to og only in the full sample (-0.81, t -5.2; ex-episode t -1.0), as an inflation mirror: headline CPI +1.03 (t 7.5), nominal wages -0.34 (t -1.4). Consumer confidence is negative and partly survives a food-CPI control ex-episode (Nordic -1.49 per SD, t -2.7). The Nordic nowcast (+6% RMSE, CW p 0.004) replicates and survives prior-year weights, real-time z-scores and stricter CPI timing. But the whole gain comes from the lagged wage term: food CPI alone gives a ratio of 1.014, and food CPI plus confidence gives 0.983. The gain disappears if real wages are lagged one more quarter (1.001). It weakens to 0.965 (p 0.04) excluding both covid and the episode.
verdicts.evidence: (a) nw_food_cpi_xvat lag 0 (CPI about 10-13 days; borderline against Orkla's Q2 report about 2 weeks after quarter end). Stress test with CPI and confidence at lag +1: 0.932 (p 0.006). (b) Confidence z-scores rebuilt with expanding-window real-time scaling plus prior-year weights: 0.939 (p 0.003). The real-wage input uses latest-vintage SE MI wages (preliminary months revised up later) and seasonally adjusted LCI. Decomposing the lagged term: headline CPI(t-1) gives 0.991; nominal wage(t-1) gives 0.961; NO-only real wage 0.958; SE-only 0.980. 2015+: 0.928. Not checked: the Granger-direction claim.
verdicts.residual_doubt: Without vintage data I cannot quantify how much SE preliminary-wage revisions inflate the lag-1 wage contribution. The fact that the gain vanishes at lag 2 is consistent with either revisions or overfitting.

verdicts.corrected_statement: The volume proxy (og minus food CPI ex VAT) falls with relative food inflation in the full sample: -0.86pp per 1pp with an India-consistent headline CPI (t -3.8), -0.70 with definition dummies. This is not separately identified from the mechanical -(1-θ) term. Holding food CPI fixed, the relative-price term is -0.64 (t -1.3) full and -0.11 (t -0.2) ex-episode, and ex-episode alone it is -0.40 (t -1.4). The only non-mechanical support is 2022-26 reported volume/mix (slope -1.0, r -0.70, n=17). Same-quarter co-movement with real income and GDP is weak (t 2.6/2.0, ns ex-episode), and the proxy is unpredictable in real time. The 4Q unemployment change at x(t-3) is a genuine but fragile OOS og predictor (ex-episode RMSE 0.949).
verdicts.evidence: (e) vol_proxy on food CPI alone: -0.45 (t -6.9). In og ~ food CPI + headline CPI ex India (ex-episode), headline CPI has coefficient 0.11 (t 0.2) vs the +0.84 the volume story implies. (d) The mechanism lens's w_food_rel_xvat_yoy subtracts an India-inclusive headline CPI from an India-exclusive food CPI over 2014Q4-22Q2. Fixing that changes -0.90 (t -4.4) to -0.86 (t -3.8), a minor effect. Unemployment (lag 1, Eurostat about 31 days, valid), OOS h=2: all 0.968; ex-episode 0.949 (CW t 5.5); ex-episode and covid 0.931; prior-year weights 0.956; fixed weights 0.944; NO+SE 0.953; Easter in base 0.956; Q3/Q4 only 0.959; strict extra lag 0.941. But x(t-2) gives 1.000, x(t-4) 0.975, 2015+ 0.977 (p 0.095), and it was the single survivor among about 4,750 tests. The r=0.83 proxy validation is not a shared-og artefact: corr(og, volume_mix) is -0.19 and a shuffled-CPI placebo gives -0.11.
verdicts.residual_doubt: Unemployment series are SA and LFS-back-cast (NO and SE redesigns in 2021). The horizon specificity suggests selection rather than structure.

verdicts.corrected_statement: corr(d_og, og(t-4)) = -0.64 is entirely mechanical: it equals the -0.65 implied by og's low lag-4 autocorrelation (0.16) alone. og-level persistence is the right d_og benchmark. Food CPI/PPI 'acceleration' does not robustly explain d_og beyond the base effect. Ex-episode the dyoy coefficient (+0.43, t 4.7) comes entirely from the yoy(t-4) component (-0.54, t -5.1; current-quarter yoy -0.04, t -0.1). With og(t-4) controlled, it drops to 0.06 (t 0.4). Full sample with the base control: 0.27 (t 2.6), episode-driven.
verdicts.evidence: (e) Identity check: actual -0.643 vs -0.651 implied from rho4=0.163, n=98 (-0.60 excluding definition-break quarters). Splitting dyoy = yoy(t) - yoy(t-4): food CPI ex VAT ex-episode gives yoy(t) -0.04 / yoy(t-4) -0.54. Food PPI: +0.62 (t 2.1) / -0.38 (t -3.1). Nordic CPI: -0.22 / -0.52. With og(t-4): food PPI dyoy 0.03 (t 0.2) ex; Nordic CPI 0.07 (t 0.4) ex. Definition-break quarters controlled with the d_og_def_break dummy and quality weights.
verdicts.residual_doubt: Food PPI keeps a positive current-quarter coefficient ex-episode (t 2.1), so some genuine same-quarter price effect may exist. It is below the honest threshold for og.

verdicts.corrected_statement: 4Q changes in Orkla-weighted policy rates lead og positively by 3-4 quarters: about +0.9-1.2pp per +1pp, t 3.5-4.3, robust to own lags, prior-year weights, covid and a coincident food-CPI control (ex-episode t 3.3-4.4). The evidence rests on two rate cycles. Excluding 2008-10 as well as 2021-23 gives t 1.5-1.9, and 2011+ ex-episode gives t 0.9-1.3. Read it as a cycle proxy, low confidence.
verdicts.evidence: (a) Policy rates are daily averages (lag 0), so timing is clean. (c) Prior-year weights: k=3 gives 1.175 (t 4.25) vs 1.168 (t 4.25). Ex-episode 0.96 (t 3.7) both ways. k=0 is not significant ex-episode (t 0.5). k=2 is borderline (t 2.7). Episode share of covariance 25%. The 2007-08 hikes lead the 2008 og highs (+4 to +6, quality-B quarters), and the 2009 cuts lead the 2010 og lows (-3 to -6).
verdicts.residual_doubt: With two cycles, timing coincidence with definition changes (2008 B start) and Orkla-specific 2010 weakness (Bakers, price pressure) cannot be excluded.

verdicts.corrected_statement: The 2021Q3-23Q4 episode dominates the strongest coincident relations: 70% of the covariance for packaging vs d_margin and for food CPI vs og. It supplies 25-37% for yields, unemployment and policy rates, and 1-13% for the lagged PPI and survey relations, so 'about half' is a median, not a rule. HAC(4) over-rejection is target-dependent. In my independent placebo (AR(1)/AR(2) regressors, no other controls), d_margin has size 3-10% (t95 1.65-2.35) and og has size 9-42% (t95 2.4-3.2, worst for near-unit-root regressors). Honest thresholds are about 2.0-2.4 for d_margin and 3.0-3.2 for og. A second episode (2007-09/2008-10) supplies most of the remaining ex-2021 evidence for raw materials, food-CPI pass-through and policy rates.
verdicts.evidence: g1_episode_share.csv and g1_placebo.csv (400 draws per design). Ex-2021 results that depend on 2007-10: raw materials (t -1.2 → -0.3), O1 (t 2.6 → 0.8), O6 (t 3.6 → 1.5-1.9). Results that do not: packaging (t -3.1 → -3.7), M3 PPI lags (t 4.5 → 4.8-5.3), M4 yields (t -3.6 → -3.4).
verdicts.residual_doubt: The robust lens calibrated placebos with feature-specific AR(2) fits and full controls (median size 17%, t95 2.72 for d_margin). My simpler placebo gives lower d_margin thresholds, so the honest d_margin threshold is uncertain within roughly 2.0-2.7.

new_findings: Timing is not where the claims fail. Every realtime_min_lag_q used for the claim variables matches the catalog release lags: EU PPI 35d (lag 1), HICP 17d (lag 1), NO/SE CPI 10-13d (lag 0), EC surveys -2d (lag 0), SSB BTS 22d (lag 1), Eurostat unemployment 31d (lag 1), LCI 77d (lag 1), FAO 6d (lag 0), daily FX and yields (lag 0). Composites take the maximum lag over their components. The only borderline case is the SE/NO CPI lag 0 against Orkla's Q2 report about 2 weeks after quarter end; a lag+1 stress test leaves the O3 nowcast gain intact (RMSE ratio 0.932).

The geographic-weight look-ahead is negligible. All composites rebuilt from country series reproduce the panel to within 1e-4. With prior-year weights (what was published before each quarter) they correlate 0.995-1.000 with the published composites, and 0.987-1.000 with fixed 2001-25 weights. Key coefficients move by at most 0.04, and OOS RMSE ratios by at most 0.01 (most within 0.003); none of the M1/M4/O1-O6 conclusions changes. Files: verify_realtime/weights_variant_diff.csv and composites_weight_variants.csv.

Base effects in y/y targets. (1) The d_og 'acceleration' effect (dyoy) is ex-episode entirely the yoy(t-4) base term (-0.54, t -5.1; current yoy -0.04). (2) EA selling-price expectations d4 → d_og at h=4 (t 5.3) collapses to t 0.9 ex-episode once og(t-4) is controlled. (3) The M3 lag-scan screen controlled d_margin(t-7), not the base d_margin(t-4). The M3 result does survive the correct base control (t 3.0-4.2), but in the 2-year margin change it shows only recovery (full t 1.3-1.4).

The M2 cost-decrease side is an M&A artefact. The delayed gain from cost decreases (+0.41 full / +1.05 ex at lag 6, quadratic PDL) turns to -0.45 / -0.24 with pure M&A dummies (Bakers, Rieber, Hame, Eastern, SladCo, Krupskaya). The Rieber 2013Q2-14Q1 dummy alone takes the full-sample value to -0.14. The fast cost-increase hit (-1.06 to -1.12pp within 1-2 quarters) is robust.

Second-episode dependence (2007-10). Outside 2021-23, the raw-material margin effect, food-CPI pass-through into og, and the policy-rate lead are each identified mainly from 2007Q2-2010Q4. The 2007 margin collapse also contains the MTR (India) and Krupskaya acquisitions and the definition-A CEE/Russia exposure; 2008 og is quality-B and is definition B's first year.

The M5 EUR/SEK OOS gain is benchmark-dependent. The PDL0-6 model beats only AR(t-1)+Easter, the base the OOS lens showed is worse than AR(t-1, t-4); against AR(t-1, t-4) the ratio is 1.007. Management-cited weak-SEK quarters (n=25) had higher d_margin (+0.36 vs -0.01pp). The text is printed in the same report as the outcome, so it can never act as a real-time predictor.

O3 Nordic og nowcast: the about 6% gain comes entirely from the lag-1 wage term, driven by the nominal wage (mostly NO LCI). A lagged headline CPI gives no gain (ratio 0.991). Lagging real wages one more quarter removes the gain (1.001). The input relies on latest-vintage, revision-prone SE MI preliminary wages and seasonally adjusted LCI.

Definition inconsistency in the mechanism lens's w_food_rel_xvat_yoy: it subtracts an India-inclusive Orkla-weighted headline CPI from an India-exclusive food CPI over 2014Q4-2022Q2. The effect on the O4 slope is small (-0.90 to -0.86). Separately, the relative-price 'volume' effect is not identified apart from the mechanical incomplete-pass-through term (ex-episode t -0.2 with food CPI controlled).

Target-side availability. Orkla's price/volume split for 2022Q2-2023Q1 comes from comparatives printed one year later; 2022Q2 is E-basis while headline og is D-basis (11.6 vs 7.4 + 3.0 = 10.4). Restricting to quarters printed in their own report (n=13), the price-on-CPI slope is 1.22 with R² 0.77. 2025 residuals average -2.6pp (CPI about 4% vs Orkla price about 1%).

Not quantifiable with the data available: the COICOP 2018 back-calculations (Eurostat HICP, SSB food CPI back to 2000-07, SCB food CPI), re-estimated seasonal factors (EC surveys, Finans Norge, LFS unemployment) and national-accounts revisions. The latest vintage is used throughout and no older vintages are stored. Back-calculation re-aggregates already-published elementary indices, so it can shift weights but not timing. d4/yoy transforms limit the effect of seasonal-factor revisions. Revisions bias most toward the coincident income/GDP and real-wage relations.

Placebo over-rejection is target-dependent. A nominal 5% HAC(4) test on d_margin rejects 3-10% of the time with persistent placebo regressors (t95 1.65-2.35), but 9-42% on og (t95 2.4-3.2). A single honest threshold of 2.7-3.0 is too strict for d_margin and too lax for og with near-unit-root regressors.
